Q1.answer: (a) Final rule 'Reduction in Force', FR Doc. 2026-15665, 91 FR 49178-49227, published Aug 3, 2026, effective Sept 2, 2026, Docket OPM-2025-0107, RIN 3206-AO86. (b) Proposed rule: FR Doc. 2026-04377, 91 FR 10904, published Mar 5, 2026 (same docket and RIN). (c) Two corrections to the main rule. (1) 2026-17335, published Aug 25, 2026 (91 FR 54794), effective Sept 2, 2026. It fixes typographical and clerical errors in the amendatory instructions and text of parts 316, 330, 351, 353 and 430. Examples: 'of this part' changed to 'of this chapter' for 5 CFR 11.2 and 11.3; list structure in 351.702(a)(4)(iv); instruction 36 on 351.802(a); instruction 39; cross-references in 351.402, 351.503, 351.506 and 351.606; and the part 351 authority citation conformed to the appeals rule (adds 5 U.S.C. 1103 and 1104). Its docket line misprints 'OPM-2026-0107'. (2) 2026-18800, published Sept 15, 2026 (91 FR 58363), effective Sept 15, 2026. It restores paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) of the definition of 'displaced' in 5 CFR 330.602. Instruction 11 of the main rule had removed them by accident. 2026-17338 (Aug 25, 2026) corrects the separate RIF Appeals rule (2026-15666), not the main rule. (d) Notices issued before Sept 2, 2026 are processed under the regulations in effect when the notice was issued. Notices issued on or after Sept 2, 2026 follow part 351 as amended. This is stated in the DATES paragraph (91 FR 49178) and in Part IV 'Implementation Considerations' (91 FR 49206-07). (e) Three other final rules amend part 351 with effect on or after Sept 2. (i) 2026-15666 'Reduction in Force Appeals' (91 FR 49230, Aug 3): it revises 351.802(a)(6) and 351.807(e), replaces subpart I (351.901-351.909), and revises the authority citation. It is effective Sept 2, 2026 and in force, but applies only to RIF actions whose specific notice issued on or after Sept 2, 2026. (ii) 2026-21320 'Administrative Leave for Workforce Realignment' (91 FR 65924, Oct 19): it revises 351.806 (status during notice period). It is effective Nov 18, 2026 and NOT yet in force on Nov 14, 2026. (iii) 2026-21316 'Managing Senior Professional Performance' (91 FR 65904, Oct 19): it revises the 351.203 definition of 'Rating of record' and reprints the authority citation. It is effective Nov 18, 2026 and NOT yet in force. 2026-13715 (Performance Appraisal, July 7, effective Aug 6) preceded the main rule's effective date. 2026-21320 and 2026-21316 are the only rules besides 2026-15666 that the CFR-part 351 filter returned; 2026-21319 (time-in-grade, effective Jan 19, 2027) does not list part 351.
Q1.uncertainty: I searched by docket, RIN and CFR part 351 and found no correction after Sept 15, 2026, but the search tool may miss one. Which rules 'amend part 351' rests on the CFR-part filter plus my reading of 2026-21316 and 2026-21320.

Q2.answer: (a) Rule: 351.503(a) assigns 7 for Level 5, 5 for Level 4, 3 for Level 3, and 0 for Levels 1 and 2, then sums the three most recent ratings. 351.503(f) fills missing ratings. 351.504 adds veterans' points. Abbott: 7+5+5 = 17; no preference, 0 points; total 17 (Subgroup B). Bianchi: 5+0+3 = 8; preference eligible with 30% or more compensable disability, +5 (AD); total 13. Castillo: 7+5+5 = 17. He is a retired member whose retired pay is based on 22 years of service, so he meets none of 351.504(b)(1), (2) or (3); the major-or-above rule in (b)(4) does not rescue him. He is not a preference eligible, so +0; total 17 (Subgroup B). Dalton: two ratings, so the proxy is (7+0)/2 = 3.5 (351.503(f)(2)); credit 3.5+7+0 = 10.5; +3 (Subgroup A); total 13.5. Eze: a 4-year term appointment is not excluded by 351.202(d), which excludes only appointments of 1 year or less, so he competes. He is in competitive service tenure subgroup II (351.502(a)(3)). Credit 5+5+5 = 15; +0; total 15. Fontaine: one rating, so 5 x 3 = 15 (351.503(f)(3)); +0; total 15. (b) Order of retention, highest to lowest: 1 Abbott 17; 2 Castillo 17; 3 Fontaine 15; 4 Eze 15; 5 Dalton 13.5; 6 Bianchi 13. Abbott and Castillo tie at 17 and are both subgroup I, so the earlier SCD ranks first (May 1, 2003 beats Aug 1, 2012; 351.501(c)). Fontaine and Eze tie at 15, so subgroup I (Fontaine) ranks ahead of subgroup II (Eze). Veterans' preference subgroups are not a ranking factor. The two lowest are released: Dalton and Bianchi. (c) Under the earlier rules, as 2026-15665 describes them, Bianchi would stand ABOVE Abbott. Employees ranked first by tenure group, then by veterans' preference subgroup AD, A, B, and only then by adjusted service date. Both are tenure group I, and Bianchi (AD) outranks Abbott (B) whatever their performance or SCDs. (d) Under 351.506(c) (and (b)(1)) she may review the complete retention register for her competitive level. It shows the names of all other listed employees, each performance credit as augmented by veterans' preference, and each SCD. She may also review the registers for other positions that could affect the composition of her level or her assignment rights (351.506(c)(2)). Access is subject to FOIA and the Privacy Act (351.506(e)).
Q2.basis: 2026-15665 reg text 351.202(d), 351.203, 351.501-351.506 (91 FR 49219-23); preamble 91 FR 49198 (description of current rules: tenure group, then AD/A/B, then adjusted service).
Q2.uncertainty: The text is silent on whether Bianchi may see the underlying ratings of other employees beyond the register entries. Whether Castillo's 22 years count toward SCD is not needed for the ranking.

Q3.answer: (a) A (Army LTC, 22 years, length-of-service retirement, no disability): not a preference eligible. 351.504(b)(1) fails (not a disability retirement), (b)(2) fails (pay based on 20 or more years), and (b)(3) fails (no continuous service since 1964); (b)(4) cannot supply a missing condition. 0 points; Subgroup B (351.504(a)(3)). B (Navy commander, 21 years, 40% disabled): also not a preference eligible, because (b)(1)-(3) are not met. Rank and disability do not help, since (b)(4) requires one of (b)(1)-(3) to be met. 0 points; Subgroup B. C (Air Force major, 14 years, disability retirement from armed conflict, 60%): preference eligible. (b)(1)(i) is met and so is (b)(2), and under (b)(4) a major or above must also be a disabled veteran, which she is. She gets +5 as 30% or more compensable disability (351.504(a)(1)); Subgroup AD. D (Army master sergeant, 24 years, no disability): not a preference eligible under (b)(2); 0 points; Subgroup B. E (staff sergeant, 16 years, medical retirement from a training injury, 10%): preference eligible under (b)(2), since retired pay is not based on 20 or more years. He is below major, so (b)(4) does not apply. He gets +3 (351.504(a)(2)); Subgroup A. (b) For A: he is not a preference eligible, so under 351.505(b)(2)(i) only active service during a war or in a campaign or expedition with an authorized badge is creditable. That is 2 years. SCD = Sept 7, 2010 minus 2 years = Sept 7, 2008. For C: she is a preference eligible, so under 351.505(b)(2)(ii) all 14 years of active service count. SCD = Sept 7, 2010 minus 14 years = Sept 7, 1996 (351.505(d)(2)). (c) The subgroups (AD, A, B) are labels shown on the retention register and in the notice (351.504(a), 351.802(a)(2)). They no longer rank employees. Ranking is by performance credit plus the veterans' points (351.501(b)); ties go to tenure subgroup and then earliest SCD (351.501(c)). The preamble says subgroups 'no longer play a predominant role' (91 FR 49204).
Q3.uncertainty: The text of 351.504(b)(5) (chapter 67 retirees) was not in play because none of the five is described as a chapter 67 retiree. Statutory definitions (5 U.S.C. 2108) are not in the Federal Register documents I read.

Q4.answer: Notice date Sept 3, 2026, so the four-year window is Sept 3, 2022 to Sept 3, 2026 (351.503(c)(1)). (a) Three most recent ratings: Aug 10, 2026 (Level 5 = 7), Nov 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3), Nov 15, 2024 (Level 3 = 3). Performance credit = 13. (b) 45 days before Sept 3 is July 20, 2026 (Sept 3 minus 31 days is Aug 3; minus 14 more days is July 20). The window is then July 20, 2022 to July 20, 2026, and the Aug 10 rating is after the cutoff. Three most recent: Nov 14, 2025 (3), Nov 15, 2024 (3), Nov 20, 2023 (4) = 3+3+5 = 11. (c) No. The cutoff is the date after which no new rating is put on record and used, and a rating must also be 'on record', meaning available to the office that builds the registers (351.503(c)(2), (c)(3)). It was put on record Aug 15, after the July 20 cutoff. (The scenario's 45-day cutoff is assumed; the rating counts only if on record by the cutoff.) (d) Aug 15, 2022 is before Sept 3, 2022, so it is outside the window. Only two ratings count: Nov 15, 2024 (Level 4 = 5) and Nov 14, 2025 (Level 3 = 3). Proxy = (5+3)/2 = 4; credit = 5+3+4 = 12 (351.503(f)(2)). (e) With no rating of record in the period, credit is 'based on the modal rating' for the summary-level pattern of his position (351.503(f)(1)).
Q4.uncertainty: (e) The definition of 'modal rating' in 351.203 is not printed in any Federal Register document I could read, and the text does not say how the modal rating converts to a credit. The most defensible reading treats it as the value of the modal rating for each of three ratings (as in (f)(3)), which would be 9 if the modal rating is Level 3. I could not establish that from the Federal Register. (c) depends on the agency's issuance defining when a rating is 'received' (351.503(c)(4)(i)).

Q5.answer: (a) (i) Notices Aug 28: the earlier rules apply, because notices issued before Sept 2 are processed under the rules in effect when issued. The RIF effective date (Oct 27) is irrelevant. Under the earlier rules performance was converted to additional years of service: 20 for an average of Level 5, 16 for Level 4, 12 for Level 3 (91 FR 49186). Lee: SCD Mar 2, 1998 minus 12 years = Mar 2, 1986. Park: July 8, 2019 minus 20 years = July 8, 1999. Same tenure group and subgroup B, so the earlier adjusted SCD ranks higher: Lee ranks higher and PARK is released. (ii) Notices Sept 2 (the effective date): the new rules apply (on or after Sept 2). Lee 3+3+3 = 9; Park 7+7+7 = 21; no preference. Park ranks higher and LEE is released. (iii) Sept 3: same as (ii); LEE is released. (b) No. Under 351.507(a) retention standing is fixed as of the date the employee receives the specific notice (Sept 3). An amended notice issued solely to state a later effective date is not a new specific notice and does not require recalculation (351.805(b)). Lee's Oct 15 Level 5 rating also post-dates the notice and the four-year window. Lee stays at 9 (Park 21); Lee is released. The agency must still correct genuine errors under 351.507(c). (c) Version of the rules: the date the agency issues the RIF notice (DATES and Part IV, 91 FR 49178, 49206-07). End of the four-year ratings period: the date of issuance of the RIF notices, or the cutoff date if the agency uses one (351.503(c)(1)-(2)). Tenure subgroup and retention standing: the date the employee receives the specific RIF notice (351.502(a)(2)-(3), (b)(2)-(3) and 351.507(a)).
Q5.uncertainty: The earlier rules are not printed; I used only the description at 91 FR 49186 (averaged, rounded, 20/16/12 years). I assumed Lee and Park are tenure group I with no tie-break issue.

Q6.answer: Jordan is a competitive service employee with a current rating of Level 2, which is enough for assignment rights (351.701(a): Level 2 or higher). His one-grade interval means three grades below GS-13 is GS-10 (351.701(b)(2), (d)). (a) He has an assignment right to positions 1 (GS-12 Ellis), 2 (GS-11 Frank) and 3 (GS-10 Gale): each is held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group, is within three grades, full-time, and in his competitive area (assuming qualification, which the facts give). The agency must offer position 1 (Ellis, GS-12), because 351.701(a) requires assignment to the position requiring 'no reduction, or the least possible reduction, in representative rate'. Not available: 4 (GS-9) is four grades below, outside the three-grade limit for him; 5 (Ito) is held by a higher-standing employee (351.701(b)(1)); 6 (Kim) is part-time, and the offered position must have the same type of work schedule (351.701(a)); 7 (Lund) is in a different competitive area (351.701(a)). (b) As a preference eligible with a compensable disability of 30% or more, his limit is five grades, so GS-9 (position 4) is also within his rights. The must-offer position is still Ellis (GS-12), the least reduction. Positions 5, 6 and 7 stay unavailable. (c) At Level 1 he has no assignment right, because 351.701(a) requires a current rating of Level 2 or higher. The agency need not offer any position, and he is released (furlough or separation). (d) If everyone is in the excepted service, 351.701 does not apply (it covers a 'competitive service tenure group employee'). Assignment rights for excepted service employees exist only if the agency chooses to adopt provisions on the same basis (351.705(a)); nothing requires an offer. If the agency adopted such provisions, the analysis would mirror (a). (e) The 2026 preamble says OPM eliminated the old 351.701(d) restriction on a Level 2 employee obtaining a position held by a higher-rated employee (91 FR 49204), so the handbook is outdated on that point. The final rule replaces the 'bump' and 'retreat' concepts with one assignment right to a position held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group (summary item 12, 91 FR 49178; 49204), and the final text of 351.701 does not use 'bump' or 'retreat'.
Q6.uncertainty: The text does not define the tie-break among several available positions beyond the 'least possible reduction' rule. Qualification under 351.702 is assumed from the facts. Whether the part-time bar has exceptions is not stated.

Q7.answer: (a) The Merit Systems Protection Board. The OPM appeals rule (2026-15666, effective Sept 2) applies only to RIF actions where the specific RIF notice issued on or after Sept 2, 2026. Morgan's notice was Aug 31, so the OPM process does not apply even though separation was Oct 30. Documents: 2026-15666 (DATES, 91 FR 49230); MSPB 2026-16456 (91 FR 51997-98), which keeps MSPB jurisdiction over RIF appeals where the notice was issued before Sept 2; 2026-15665 (DATES: earlier rules apply to notices before Sept 2); 2026-17338 (correction to the appeals rule; it changes no applicability). Caveat: 2026-16456 also says (91 FR 51998) it will adjudicate RIF appeals in which the RIF effective date preceded Sept 2 (see uncertainty). (b) OPM hears it (351.901(a)), not MSPB. She must file electronically through the e-filing system identified on OPM's website; email and postal filings are not accepted absent good cause (351.902(a), (c)). Deadline: 30 calendar days from the Dec 18 effective date; day 1 is Dec 19, so day 30 is Sunday Jan 17, 2027. Monday Jan 18, 2027 is the Martin Luther King Jr. federal holiday, so the period runs to the first workday, Tuesday Jan 19, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (351.902(b), (b)(1)). (c) She must prove by a preponderance: (1) timeliness; (2) OPM jurisdiction; (3) the agency failed to comply with an applicable statute or OPM RIF regulation; and (4) the failure prejudiced her, causing the action or loss of a materially more favorable outcome (351.901(b)). No hearing as of right: review is on the written record unless OPM determines a hearing is 'necessary and efficient' (record insufficiently developed on a material fact, or a material credibility dispute) (351.905(c)). (d) The rule says the part 351 procedures are the sole and exclusive means of appealing a RIF action, and a RIF action and any matter relating to an appeal 'may not be raised under a negotiated grievance procedure or contested through grievance arbitration' (351.901(c)(1)-(2)). The preamble says the final rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs or adjudicate CBA disputes, and that when agreements are renegotiated the rule will limit agencies' duty and ability to bargain for a RIF appeal process inconsistent with part 351 (91 FR 49245). (e) No. 351.901(c)(4) says a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under this subpart, and 351.909(e) says there is no further right of appeal of OPM's final decision. Collateral matters before EEOC, an IG, MSPB, DOL VETS or OSC are preserved (351.901(c)(3)). (f) Yes. Under 351.902(b)(3), a collateral complaint timely filed before the filing period expired (the OSC complaint) whose final decision materially affects retention standing allows a RIF appeal within 30 calendar days after the decision becomes final and no longer subject to further administrative review. If final on Mar 10, 2027, 30 days gives Friday Apr 9, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET. OPM decides, in its sole and exclusive discretion, whether the decision materially affects her rights. (g) The DATES paragraph of 2026-15666 (91 FR 49230, first page): 'This final rule applies only to a RIF action for which an agency issues the employee a specific RIF notice under 5 CFR 351.802 on or after September 2, 2026.' The MSPB rule's DATES and Part B (91 FR 51997) track this.
Q7.uncertainty: The MSPB rule is internally inconsistent: Part B and its first DATES sentence key MSPB jurisdiction to the notice date, while a later sentence (91 FR 51998) keys it to the RIF effective date. On that sentence an Oct 30 separation would fall outside MSPB's stated coverage. I follow 2026-15666 and the notice-date statements. The Jan 18, 2027 holiday status comes from my calendar knowledge, not the Federal Register. The old MSPB appeal regulations are not printed in these documents.

Q8.answer: (a) In force today: the earlier text of 351.806 is not printed in the 2026 documents. OPM describes its paragraph (a) as saying the employee stays in a duty status 'when possible' (91 FR 65926, 65933). Adopted but not yet in force: 2026-21320, effective Nov 18, 2026, revises 351.806 in full. (a) 'Under ordinary circumstances, an employee will remain in a duty status during the notice period.' (b) 'Nothing in this section precludes an agency from placing an employee on administrative leave for all or part of the notice period when the agency determines that such leave is appropriate and the use of administrative leave is consistent with part 630, subpart N.' (c) restates the emergency lack of work or funds rule (annual leave with or without consent; LWOP only with consent; nonpay status without consent). (b) No consent is required. 351.806(b) has no consent condition, and new 5 CFR 630.1403(c)(10) permits administrative leave for employees facing involuntary RIF separation between notice receipt and separation 'when the agency determines it is in the Government's best interests'. The preamble says 'provide' covers leave with or without consent (91 FR 65933). Neither paragraph states a duration limit. Unlike (c)(9) and (c)(11), (c)(10) has no 'subject to Governmentwide limits' parenthetical. The preamble says agency limits operate within the Governmentwide limit, currently 12 weeks per instance for workforce realignment initiatives under the OPM template (91 FR 65935), and that the 10-workday statutory cap applies to investigative leave. Oct 26 to Dec 18 is 53 days (about 7.6 weeks). (c) OPM says its policy guidance (Template for Agency Administrative Leave Policies, CPM 2025-12, July 30, 2025, section D.1.b) already provided that an authorized agency official may provide administrative leave between receipt of a separation notice and the effective date (91 FR 65926). (d) No. OPM says 351.806 and 630.1403(c)(10) address only paid non-duty status, and retention registers, retention standing, veterans' preference, other RIF requirements and appeal rights continue to apply in full (91 FR 65925-26).
Q8.uncertainty: The pre-Nov 18 text of 351.806 is not printed in the Federal Register documents. Whether the 12-week Governmentwide limit governs RIF-notice leave under (c)(10) is not stated. Today (Nov 14) the adopted text is not yet in force; the leave began Oct 26, before it takes effect, so it rests on OPM guidance as OPM characterizes it.

Q9.answer: Steps NOT in compliance: 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 12. In order: 2, 7, 9. Step 1: noncompliant. A competitive area established or materially modified within 90 days before the notices (Aug 17 to Oct 13 is 57 days) must be described to OPM, with a written statement of its bona fide organizational basis, for approval in advance (351.402(c)). Nothing was sent. (Designation by the head or designee is allowed, but not below headquarters level, 351.402(b)(1).) Step 2: in order. A career-conditional employee in an initial probationary period is not a competing employee, and the agency may retain her while releasing a competing employee (351.202(d)(2)(ii), (d)(3)). Step 3: noncompliant. 'Initial probationary period' excludes the supervisory or managerial probationary period (351.203). Ortiz is a career employee, in tenure subgroup I and a competing employee (351.202(d), 351.502(a)(2)), and must be ranked. Step 4: noncompliant. The cutoff is Oct 13 minus 30 days = Sept 13, 2026. A rating put on record Oct 2 is after the cutoff and cannot be used, and ratings must be applied uniformly in the competitive area (351.503(c)(2), (c)(4)). Step 5: noncompliant. With two ratings the proxy is (7+5)/2 = 6, so credit is 6+7+5 = 18, not 15 (351.503(f)(2)). Step 6: noncompliant. Additional performance points are available only under 351.503(d) for single-pattern systems whose highest level is Level 3 (pass/fail or pattern D), and under (e) for multiple patterns. A five-level pattern gets the 7/5/3/0/0 credit only (351.503(a), (d); 430.208(e)(4)). Step 7: in order. If employees are tied on credit, subgroup and service dates, the agency may select any tied employee (351.601(c)). Step 8: noncompliant. An agency may not release a competing employee while retaining in the level an employee on a specifically limited temporary or term promotion (351.602(a)). Step 9: in order. The assessment is not required if, in the 5 years ending on the notice date, the employee occupied the same position and received Level 3 or higher in it (351.702(a)(4)(v)); Silva held it until 2023 with a 2022 Level 4. Step 10: noncompliant. Qualification must use an assessment that is based on a job analysis and allows demonstration of job-related skills, and that does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment (351.702(a)(4)(i)-(iii)). Step 11: noncompliant. Each temporary exception stands alone and may not be sequenced or stacked (351.608(a)(3)). The agency may apply only the one with the longest period, and the undue-interruption exception is capped at 90 days (351.608(b)); (g) is capped at 90 days. The agency cannot give 60 + 60 = 120 days. Retention over 30 days also needs written notice to higher-standing employees and a register entry (351.608(a)(4)). Step 12: noncompliant. Notices issued on or after Sept 2, 2026 must state the right to appeal to OPM, the time limit under 351.902(b), and the electronic filing system on OPM's website (351.802(a)(6) as amended by 2026-15666). The appeal is to OPM, not MSPB, filed within 30 calendar days from the effective date: Dec 14 + 30 = Jan 13, 2027, 11:59 p.m. ET (351.902(b)).
Q9.uncertainty: Step 1: the designation by 'the agency head's designee' is acceptable only if the designee is at headquarters level; the write-up does not say. Step 9 assumes Silva is otherwise entitled to the offered position. Step 12 assumes the Dec 14 effective date and that Jan 13, 2027 is a workday (it is a Wednesday).

Q10.answer: (a) On Sept 10, 2026, paragraph (1) of the definition of 'displaced' in 5 CFR 330.602 contained only its introductory text: 'A current competitive service employee in the competitive service tenure group at grade GS-15 (or equivalent) or below (or another qualifying competitive service appointment, as determined by OPM) who:'. Sub-paragraphs (1)(i) and (1)(ii) were absent, because amendatory instruction 11 of the main rule (2026-15665, 91 FR 49217) set out only the introductory text and so deleted them by accident (see 2026-18800). (b) On Sept 15, 2026, 2026-18800 (91 FR 58363, effective Sept 15) revised paragraph (1) in its entirety, restoring (i) (a RIF separation notice under part 351 without having declined a qualifying offer) and (ii) (a notice of proposed removal under part 752 for declining a directed relocation outside the commuting area) as they read before the final rule. OPM invoked 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) good cause to skip notice and comment because the document 'makes no substantive change'; it restores text in effect before Sept 2 that OPM did not propose to remove and the final rule did not discuss removing. It made the correction effective on publication under 553(d)(3). It styled the action a 'correcting amendment'. (c) Restored (1)(i) makes an employee 'displaced' if she received a RIF separation notice and 'has not declined an offer under part 351, subpart G, of a position with the same type of work schedule and a representative rate at least as high as that of the position from which the employee will be separated'. If Nadia declines a full-time offer with a LOWER representative rate, that is not a qualifying offer, so she is still displaced. If the declined offer had the SAME representative rate (full-time), she has declined a qualifying offer and is no longer displaced under (1)(i).
Q10.uncertainty: The pre-Sept 15 text of (1)(i)-(ii) is shown only as restored by 2026-18800. Paragraph (1)(ii) and any CTAP eligibility effects of the gap between Sept 2 and Sept 15 are not addressed by OPM.

Q11.answer: Differences between the proposed (2026-04377, 91 FR 10926-34) and final (2026-15665, 91 FR 49218-27) part 351 text. 351.202(d): heading changed from 'Employees excluded. The provisions of this part do not apply to...' to 'Employees excluded from reduction in force competition'. (d)(1)(ii) and (d)(2)(i)-(ii): the phrases 'as of the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice' are dropped. (d)(2)(iii): 'temporary or term appointment of 1 year or less under subpart C or D of part 316' became 'temporary appointment of one year or less under subpart D of part 316'. (d)(3): proposed said such employees may be retained, furloughed, separated, demoted or reassigned 'without regard to the provisions of this part'; final says without determining retention standing, applying subpart F order of release or subpart G assignment rights, provided the action is consistent with the appointment and law. New (d)(4) adds a written-notice requirement. 351.202(c)(3): typo 'such the reclassification' fixed. 351.203: final adds 'Restoration protected employee'; 'Initial probationary period' excludes the supervisory or managerial probation (subpart I of part 315). 351.204: not in proposal as amended (merit system principles added). 351.302 (transfer of function): final adds a new paragraph (d) (adverse action procedures if the employee declines to transfer) and re-letters later paragraphs. 351.402(b)(1): same text; new (c) (OPM approval for new or modified competitive areas within 90 days of notices). 351.502(a)(2)-(3), (b)(2)-(3): 'the date the agency issues a specific reduction in force notice' became 'the date the employee receives a specific reduction in force notice'; (a)(3) 'subpart C or D of part 316' became 'subpart D of part 316'. 351.503(a)(1): cross-reference to 5 CFR 430.208(d) became 430.208(e); 'Minimally Successful' became 'Minimally Satisfactory'. 351.504(a)(1)-(3): 'should be identified' became 'must be identified' for Subgroups AD, A and B. 351.505(b)(2): 'covered by Sec. 351.503(b)' became 'covered by Sec. 351.504(b)' (cross-reference to the right section). 351.506(c)(1): 'their performance credit' and 'their service computation dates' (all listed employees) became 'the employee's performance credit' and 'the employee's service computation date'. 351.506(d): final adds that the paragraph does not limit access under another statute or regulation. 351.507(b): 'any of this paragraph (b)' became 'any of these provisions'. 351.604: proposed revised (b) and removed (d); the final makes no change to 351.604. 351.605: moved to a structure with (a) appropriate use, (b), (c) notice (with 351.802(a)(1), (3), (5), (6) and (b) content and a statement of abolishment), and (d) retention register not required; 'excluded from the provisions of this part' became 'excluded from reduction in force competition'; 'may not apply assignment rights' became 'must not'. 351.606(a): proposed one sentence citing 'Sec. 351.209(b)' (priority over other competing employees); final is a six-paragraph USERRA mandatory exception citing 'Sec. 353.209(b)'. 351.701(a): 'minimally successful (Level 2)' became 'minimally satisfactory (Level 2)'. 351.702(a)(4)(iii): 'Does not solely include or principally rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination' became 'Does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment'; new (a)(4)(v) (5-year same-position exemption). 351.802(a): final adds introductory text; (a)(2) 'veteran status' became 'veterans' preference subgroup'. 351.805(b): final amends (not in proposal). Parts 353 and 362: the final adds 353.110, 353.209(a) and 362.306(a) changes and drops 362.205 wording differences; I did not compare every word of those.
Q11.uncertainty: I did not read every word of proposed 351.503(d)-(f), 351.608(c)-(e), or parts 316, 330, 353, 359, 362 and 430 side by side, so other differences may exist. The list is complete only for the passages named.

Q12.answer: (a) Notice Oct 5, 2026, no cutoff; window Oct 5, 2022 to Oct 5, 2026. Quinn: career-conditional in an initial probationary period, so not a competing employee and not on the register (351.202(d)(2)(ii)). Alvarez: 5,5,4 = 7+7+5 = 19; +0; total 19 (tenure I). Chen: the Sept 30, 2022 rating is before the window, so two ratings (Level 5, Level 4); proxy (7+5)/2 = 6; credit 6+7+5 = 18; +0; total 18 (tenure I). Dube: two ratings 4,4; proxy (5+5)/2 = 5; credit 15; +3 (A); total 18 (tenure II). Estrada: the Oct 20, 2026 Level 5 is after the notice date and unusable; three most recent: Nov 2025 (4), Nov 2024 (3), Nov 2023 (4) = 5+3+5 = 13; +3 = 16. Brandt: 3,4,2 = 3+5+0 = 8; +5 (AD, 30% disabled) = 13. Farouk: one rating (Level 3): 3 x 3 = 9; +0 = 9. Order: Alvarez 19; Chen 18; Dube 18 (Chen first: subgroup I before II); Estrada 16; Brandt 13; Farouk 9. (b) Seven positions less three abolished leaves four; Quinn holds one, so three of the six competing employees stay. Farouk was restored on July 13, 2026 after 14 months (more than 180 days) of uniformed service, so he is a restoration protected employee for one year (351.203, 351.606(a), 353.209(b) as described at 91 FR 49203). He may not be released while another competing employee can be released instead; his ordinary standing is still computed (lowest, 9). Released: Brandt (13), Estrada (16), and Dube (18, the lowest ranked employee after skipping Farouk). Retained: Alvarez, Chen, Farouk (plus Quinn). (c) Assignment is to a position held by a lower-standing employee in the same tenure group, within three grades (five for a 30%-disabled preference eligible), the least reduction in rate (351.701). Standing compares total credit then tenure subgroup then SCD. Gomez 17, Hill 5+3+3 = 11 + 3 = 14, Jones 5+5+5 = 15, Ikeda 3+3+3 = 9. Dube (18) outranks Gomez (17): offer GS-12 Gomez (least reduction); Hill and Jones also lower but a greater reduction; Ikeda is four grades down, outside his limit. Estrada (16): Gomez 17 is higher; Hill (14), Jones (15) and Ikeda (9) are lower; Ikeda is GS-9, four grades below and outside his three-grade limit; offer GS-11 Hill (least reduction) and not Jones. Brandt (13): Gomez 17, Hill 14 and Jones 15 are all higher; only Ikeda (9) is lower, and GS-9 is four grades down, within Brandt's five-grade limit as a 30% disabled preference eligible; offer GS-9 Ikeda. (d) Gomez, Hill and Ikeda are displaced and are each qualified only for their own positions, so they have no further assignment right and are separated. Jones is untouched. Alvarez, Chen, Farouk and Quinn stay at GS-13; Dube takes GS-12, Estrada GS-11, Brandt GS-9.
Q12.uncertainty: The text of 353.209(b) (the 6-month/1-year protection) is not printed in any document I read; I relied on the preamble's description of 38 U.S.C. 4316(c). Whether Farouk's protection would extend to being passed over rather than reassigned is as 351.606(a)(2) states. Estrada's 'current rating of record' for assignment is Level 4 or 5; either meets the Level 2 floor.

Q13.answer: Preamble statements that differ from the regulatory text in 2026-15665: (1) Erosion-of-duties reclassification. Preamble (91 FR 49190): OPM removes the reclassification from the RIF list only 'if the action would take effect after an agency had formally announced a RIF in the employee's competitive area and the RIF would take effect within 180 days'. Text 351.202(c)(3) (91 FR 49218): such reclassifications are exempt, but the agency may not undertake one 'between the time an agency has formally announced a reduction in force ... and the completion of the reduction in force' where it would adversely affect retention standing; no 180-day condition. The summary (91 FR 49178, item 8) and the later passage at 49190 ('between the formal announcement and completion') state the text's version. (2) Transfer of function. Preamble (91 FR 49195): 'OPM is revising Sec. 351.302(b) to state that, except as permitted in paragraph (e), the losing agency must use the adverse action procedures found in 5 CFR part 752'. Text (91 FR 49219): that rule is in 351.302(d); (b) deals with employees transferred to a function terminating within 60 days. No other preamble passage corrects it. (3) Part 353. Preamble (91 FR 49206): 'OPM is revising Sec. 353.301(b) to provide more information about how retention protections ... operate during a RIF'. Text (91 FR 49226-27): no 353.301(b) is revised; 353.301(a) is revised to replace 'tenure group III', and the retention content is in 353.209(a) and 351.606. The same section's later paragraph (49206, 'removing a reference to tenure group III in Sec. 353.301(a)') and the passage at 49203 (353.209(a)) state it correctly. (4) Assessments. Preamble (91 FR 49204): the assessment 'does not rely on a self-assessment from an automated examination'. Text 351.702(a)(4)(iii) (91 FR 49226): 'does not consist solely of, or principally rely on, an automated self-assessment'. The text is narrower than the preamble. The passage at 49206 ('reduces overreliance on automated self-assessments') matches the text. The same preamble point also reappears in 330.213(c)(1) ('does not principally rely'), which is inconsistent with 330.202(5)(iii) ('solely ... or principally') (91 FR 49216-17).
Q13.uncertainty: I read most of the section-by-section analysis (subparts B to G, parts 330, 353, 359, 362, 430) but not the long economic and regulatory-alternatives sections. Item (1) turns on reading the 180-day sentence as describing the rule rather than the old rule; the preamble phrasing is ambiguous. Other mismatches may exist.

Q14.answer: (i) Preamble versus text of OPM's appeals rule (2026-15666 as corrected by 2026-17338). (A) Judicial review: preamble (91 FR 49242) says the final rule 'provides that a party cannot obtain judicial review of a decision under part 351'; text 351.901(c)(4) (91 FR 49264) says 'under this subpart'. (B) Existing CBAs: preamble (91 FR 49245) says the rule does not retroactively invalidate existing CBAs and operates when agreements are renegotiated; text 351.901(c)(2) (91 FR 49263) flatly bars raising a RIF action or related matter under a negotiated grievance procedure, with no exception for existing agreements. (C) Representatives: the summary of changes (91 FR 49231) says OPM 'or the responsible agency' may disallow a representative; as corrected, 351.904(c) says 'the agency whose action is under appeal' (2026-17338, 91 FR 54796). (ii) Changes from the proposal not acknowledged in the summary of changes (91 FR 49230-32): (A) the proposed 351.901(c) said the procedures supersede appeal procedures in agency policies or collective bargaining agreements; the final drops that sentence (the summary mentions only the new grievance bar). (B) The proposed list of entities with preserved independent jurisdiction included the Federal Labor Relations Authority; the final list (EEOC, IG, MSPB, DOL VETS, OSC) omits it, which the summary does not mention (91 FR 49263-64 vs 5875). (C) Proposed 351.802(a)(6) ended 'The agency must also comply with Sec. 1201.21 of this title' (MSPB notice rules); the final drops that sentence, while the summary mentions only the added time-limit and e-filing detail (91 FR 49263 vs 5874). (D) 351.903(b)(1): agency response due 'within 30 calendar days of the initial appeal' became 'after service of the initial appeal'. (E) 351.902(c)(2): final adds 'or exempted under paragraph (c)(7) of this section for good cause'; 351.902(c)(5): 'best address' became 'address'. (F) 351.905(c): proposed allowed 'a hearing or any other appropriate action' and directing parties to comply; the final keeps only a hearing. (G) 351.906(b): 'OPM shall' became 'OPM may' draw inferences or impose sanctions, and a new 351.906(c) limits sanctions to proportionate ones; the summary does not mention either. (H) The authority citation for part 351 changed (adds 5 U.S.C. 1103, 1104, 2301 and 38 U.S.C. 4331). (iii) The Board's rule (2026-16456, 91 FR 51997-98) is inconsistent about which RIF appeals it will still hear: its DATES says it will not apply the rule to 'newly filed cases relating to agency actions taken before the effective date of OPM's rulemakings'; Part B says it will accept appeals 'where the agency's RIF notice was issued before the rule's effective date'; a later sentence says it will adjudicate RIF appeals received after Sept 2 'in which the RIF effective date preceded September 2, 2026'. OPM's rule (91 FR 49230) turns on whether the notice issued on or after Sept 2. A RIF noticed before Sept 2 but effective after Sept 2 is covered by the MSPB's Part B and OPM's DATES but not by its last sentence.
Q14.uncertainty: I compared the proposed and final regulatory text paragraph by paragraph. I did not read all of the final rule's section-by-section analysis, so other preamble/text mismatches may exist. Items (ii)(D), (E), (F) and (G) are real textual changes, but a reader could say the summary covers them generally ('more flexible', 'narrower'). The Board rule's 'agency actions taken' phrase is ambiguous.
